messages:
olivia: FYI - during the vuln sweep we rolled the TLS hardening config (drop RSA/ecc-legacy ciphers, enforce TLS1.3-only) and simultaneously applied a keystore RBAC tidy. Now the cert-mint service in sa-east-1 is failing to issue ephemeral mTLS certs -> downstream services can't establish mutual TLS. This looks like a KMS signing permission problem, not just cipher mismatch. 

raj: Any KMS error examples? which key?

kevin: Paste from mint-service logs (sa-east-1):
```
2026-03-23T02:12:05Z mint-01 error=asymmetricSign DENY key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/signing/cryptoKeys/signing-key-v1 reason=permissionDenied principal=svc-account:mint-service@prod
stack=crypto/sign:signer.go:142
```
Request to /mint returned 502: cert sign failed
```

olivia: Confirmed. That key is the region-global signing key used by the ephemeral cert endpoint. The RBAC tidy removed `roles/cloudkms.signer` from service accounts that were flagged as inactive in the EU org. sa-east accounts got caught in the filter.

deploy-bot: policy-prune "keystore-prune-2026-03-23" applied by @raj at 2026-03-23T02:05:11Z. Suggested action: rollback if production crypto ops fail.

raj: Rolling back the prune now, will re-run with explicit whitelist exceptions for active principals. Rolling back is fastest to recover.

kevin: While rollback is in flight, can mint-service fall back to local ephemeral keys (software) for low-volume tenants? There's a flag `--soft-fallback=enabled` but it was off. If we enable it we avoid outage but with lower crypto protections. Thoughts?

olivia: Prefer not to enable software fallback in prod without approval. Rollback and then patch policy to add region exceptions. Also need to treat KMS sign denies as high priority.

raj: RBAC rolled back at 02:18 UTC. KMS audit now shows asymmetricsign success for mint-service principals. Services recovered.

kevin: Confirmed mint-service metrics back to normal within 90s. Will keep `--soft-fallback` toggle prepared as emergency runbook step (commented).

olivia: P1 mitigated. Follow-ups: 
- Create an automated check in policy CI to call `gcloud kms keys test-iam-permissions signing-key-v1 --permissions=kms.cryptoKeys.asymmetricSign` for all mint-service principals across regions.
- Add an alert on KMS audit logs for AsymmetricSign DENY spikes (threshold: >3 denies / 5m).
- Add a preflight in the TLS hardening rollout: verify that all cert-issuers can perform asymmetricSign against their configured key before applying ciphers.
- Document temporary fallback policy and approval flow for `--soft-fallback` (who can flip it and when).

ci-bot: CI pipeline note: opened ticket CI-513 for policy test addition, assigned to @kevin.

sec-oncall: Opening incident INC-5678 and scheduling 45m RCA. Please attach policy-diff and KMS audit exports for the window 02:00-02:30 UTC. Also escalate to compliance for vuln triage notes: we toggled TLS config during active keystore changes, that's a risky combined-change pattern.

olivia: Agree. Action item: avoid performing simultaneous crypto policy changes (TLS config) and RBAC prunes. Add a gated change rule in deploy calendar requiring a 24h window between keystore RBAC changes and TLS hardening rollouts.

raj: I'll update the deploy gating. Also will add an automated 'sign test' job that runs as part of the `policy-prune` job and fails the job if any principal returns DENY. Drafting MR now.

kevin: Quick mitigation idea for future: mint-service could cache the CA-signed template for 5m and reuse existing keys for short-lived calls when KMS is unavailable; will prototype as a low-risk improvement.

olivia: Good. Assigning owners: @raj - policy gating and RBAC CI checks; @kevin - alert + cache prototype; @sec-oncall - incident runbook update to include KMS.AsymmetricSign as a pagerable signal.

deploy-bot: Incident INC-5678 created by @sec-oncall. All change and audit artifacts are being archived to /incidents/5678/

olivia: Thanks team. Final note: treat KMS sign permissions separately from unwrap permissions in our alerting taxonomy. They represent different failure modes for mTLS (cert issuance vs key unwrap for existing certs).
